ECS Fargate Overview
AWS ECS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers. It removes the need to provision and manage servers. You define your application as a task definition. Fargate handles the infrastructure automatically. This reduces operational overhead significantly. Developers can focus on building applications rather than managing clusters.

Task definitions specify container images and resource requirements. Each task definition includes CPU units and memory allocations. Network mode determines how containers communicate. The awsvpc network mode gives each task its own elastic network interface. IAM roles can be attached at the task level for AWS API access. Logging configuration sends container output to CloudWatch. Environment variables can be injected from AWS Secrets Manager. Volumes can be mounted for persistent storage or configuration files. Health check configurations monitor container responsiveness. Timeout values determine how long Fargate waits before marking a task unhealthy.

Service auto-scaling adjusts the number of running tasks automatically. It uses target tracking policies based on CloudWatch metrics. CPU utilization is the most common scaling metric. Memory utilization can also trigger scaling events. Application Load Balancer request counts provide another scaling signal. Custom metrics from the application can be published to CloudWatch. Scale-out occurs when the metric exceeds the target threshold. Scale-in occurs when the metric drops below the threshold for a sustained period.

Step scaling policies apply predefined adjustments to task counts. Each step defines a metric range and a scaling adjustment. The adjustment specifies how many tasks to add or remove. Cooldown periods prevent rapid fluctuations in task count. Warm-up periods give new tasks time to start processing requests. Multiple step adjustments can be configured for different severity levels. Fine-grained scaling provides precise control over capacity. Broad adjustment ranges handle sudden traffic spikes quickly.

Scheduled scaling adjusts capacity based on predictable patterns. Daily schedules handle morning traffic peaks for business applications. Weekly schedules prepare for weekend marketing campaigns. Monthly schedules accommodate billing cycles and report generation. Cron expressions define when the scaling action should trigger. Recurring schedules maintain a minimum capacity during business hours. One-time schedules prepare capacity for planned events like product launches. Timezone configuration ensures schedules align with business hours across regions.

Unified Score System
The Unified Score is a composite metric measuring retrieval pipeline quality. It combines five weighted components into a single value between zero and one. The formula uses Retrieval at 0.25 weight and Quality at 0.35 weight. Faithfulness contributes 0.25 to the overall score. Latency penalty subtracts 0.10 times the normalized latency value. Cost penalty subtracts 0.05 times the normalized cost value. The final score is clamped between zero and one inclusive.

Retrieval quality measures how well the system finds relevant documents. Recall at five determines what percentage of relevant documents appear in the top five results. Mean reciprocal rank evaluates the position of the first relevant result. Context precision measures whether retrieved passages contain useful information. Hybrid retrieval combining dense vectors and keyword search improves recall. Cross-encoder reranking further refines the top twenty candidates down to five.

Faithfulness evaluation checks whether generated answers are factually grounded. The evaluator compares the generated answer against the retrieved context. Any claim not supported by the context reduces the faithfulness score. A score below 0.5 blocks deployment regardless of other metrics. This is a non-bypassable safety gate in the system. Adversarial testing uses unanswerable questions to verify the pipeline does not fabricate responses. Ten hand-crafted adversarial questions form the benchmark suite.

The RAGAS framework provides additional granular metrics for evaluation. Context precision measures what fraction of retrieved chunks is relevant. Context recall determines if all necessary information was retrieved. Answer relevancy checks if the generated answer addresses the query. Faithfulness measures factual consistency with the source context. These metrics feed into the Diagnoser agent for targeted improvement recommendations. Each metric contributes to identifying specific failure types in the retrieval pipeline.

The Evaluator agent runs the three-layer evaluation stack automatically. Layer one computes the Unified Score from the five weighted components. Layer two runs RAGAS metrics for detailed quality diagnostics. Layer three executes adversarial testing with unanswerable questions. All three layers must pass for a pipeline to be deployment eligible. Results are written to the evaluations table with full metric breakdowns. Judge reasoning provides a one-sentence explanation for each score. This reasoning helps the Diagnoser classify failures into the five-type taxonomy.

Retrieval Failure Modes
The Diagnoser agent classifies failures into five distinct types. Retrieval Miss occurs when relevant documents are not found in the top results. Context Overflow happens when retrieved context exceeds the LLM token budget. Hallucination is flagged when generated answers lack factual grounding. Answer Incompleteness means the answer does not fully address the user query. Latency Spike indicates the response time exceeded performance thresholds. Each failure type maps to specific remediation strategies.

For Retrieval Miss, the Improver increases the k-value for retrieval. It may also switch from dense-only to hybrid retrieval. Adjusting the chunk size can improve recall for certain document types. Changing the embedding model sometimes helps with semantic matching. Reducing the similarity threshold broadens the candidate pool. Adding query rewriting before retrieval improves query quality.

For Context Overflow, the Improver reduces the chunk size parameter. The Compressor agent can truncate context more aggressively. Adjusting the reranker top-k reduces the number of candidates. Setting a lower token budget for the LLM call helps. Pre-filtering chunks by relevance score eliminates noise. Summarization before generation condenses the retrieved context.

For Hallucination, the Improver switches to a stricter prompt template. Adding negative constraints prevents the model from inventing facts. Reducing the temperature parameter makes generation more deterministic. Using a larger context window provides more factual grounding. Enabling chain-of-thought reasoning improves answer accuracy. Switching to a more capable LLM sometimes resolves persistent hallucination cases. The faithfulness hard block at 0.5 ensures hallucinating pipelines never deploy.

For Answer Incompleteness, the Improver increases retrieval count to gather more context. Expanding the chunk size captures more surrounding information. Adding query decomposition breaks complex questions into sub-questions. Multi-hop retrieval chains multiple search operations together. The HyDE technique generates hypothetical answers for better retrieval. Increasing the generation token budget allows more comprehensive answers.

For Latency Spike, the Improver reduces the reranker candidate count. Switching to a faster embedding model reduces vector computation time. Caching frequently retrieved chunks avoids repeated operations. Reducing the retrieval count minimizes vector search operations. Using a smaller LLM for generation trades quality for speed. Pre-computing embeddings for static documents eliminates runtime costs.

Deployment Architecture
ECS Fargate tasks run in isolated VPC subnets for security. The Application Load Balancer distributes traffic across tasks. Health checks monitor task responsiveness via HTTP endpoints. Auto-scaling policies maintain service availability during traffic spikes. AWS WAF provides protection against common web vulnerabilities. Shield Advanced adds DDoS protection for critical workloads. CloudWatch metrics and logs provide operational visibility. X-Ray tracing enables distributed request tracing across services.

Blue-green deployments minimize downtime during updates. The green environment runs the new version while blue serves production traffic. The Deployer agent performs a gradual weight shift from blue to green. Health checks validate the green environment before full traffic cutover. Auto-rollback triggers if error rates exceed one percent during canary. Rollback also triggers if p95 latency exceeds three seconds. The ten-minute canary window provides sufficient observation time. Immutable SHA-tagged Docker images ensure reproducible deployments.

The pipeline lifecycle manages document ingestion through deployment. Ingestion parses raw documents and applies PII masking. Chunking strategies segment documents into retrievable units. The Builder embeds chunks and creates vector index structures. The Evaluator computes quality scores for the indexed pipeline. The Observer monitors production metrics for quality drift. The Diagnoser identifies failure root causes from observation data. The Improver generates alternative configurations for better performance. The Deployer manages the promotion of approved changes to production.

Supabase provides the unified data platform for the entire system. PostgreSQL handles relational data including pipeline configurations and evaluation results. The pgvector extension enables similarity search over embeddings. Each pipeline version gets its own isolated vector table. The naming convention uses autorag underscore pipeline identifier underscore version. Storage buckets hold raw documents and chunk artifacts. Row-level security enforces multi-tenant data isolation. The audit log table is insert-only with eleven distinct event types.

Monitoring and observability are critical for production RAG systems. Prometheus scrapes metrics from FastAPI and LangGraph worker endpoints. Grafana dashboards visualize pipeline quality trends over time. Alert rules trigger when error rates exceed defined thresholds. P95 latency monitoring detects performance degradation early. Cost tracking ensures LLM API spending stays within budget. The Observer agent continuously monitors deployed pipeline health. Structured logs include X-Trace-ID for distributed tracing context. Metric cardinality is managed to prevent time-series database explosion. SLO dashboards show compliance with availability and latency targets.

Security controls span multiple layers of the platform. Custom PII Detection and Masking Functions run at the ingestion boundary. Detected PII is masked before any data reaches storage or LLMs. Prompt injection defenses prevent adversarial manipulation of the system. Input validation and output schema enforcement add additional guardrails. JWT authentication secures all API endpoints with organization-level scoping. AWS Secrets Manager stores API keys and database credentials. Network isolation through VPC private subnets prevents external access. Immutable audit logs track all pipeline creation and deployment events. Faithfulness hard blocks prevent hallucinating pipelines from reaching production. Adversarial testing continuously validates safety properties of the system.
